name: WM-FTT working memory strategies data (v1/v2/v3), participant- and stimulus-level exports
description: Data from the Working Memory Feature Trade-off Task (WM-FTT): word, orientation and colour recall under a parity-judgement distractor, pooled across three task versions (v1 original, v2 added a parity-error penalty, v3 added recall-order randomisation). Two datasets are described here: all_data_surveys (one row per participant: demographics, questionnaire scores, and raw questionnaire/strategy items) and all_data_full (one row per stimulus: trial structure, targets, responses, timing, and per-feature recall scores; no questionnaire item detail, see all_data_surveys for that). NAMING NOTE: the task was called CFA-WM during data collection, and column names, OSF component names and the front-end code still use that prefix (for example strats_cfa_q01_colors_1). Those identifiers are deliberately unchanged so that this export remains byte-comparable with earlier ones and with the raw JATOS data. WM-FTT and CFA-WM refer to the same task.
citation: WM-FTT (formerly CFA-WM) v1/v2/v3, Mael Delem, EMC Lab, Universite Lumiere Lyon 2
creditText: VVIQ item text: Marks, D. F. (1973). Visual imagery differences in the recall of pictures. British Journal of Psychology, 64(1), 17-24. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2044-8295.1973.tb01322.x

OSIVQ item text: Blazhenkova, O., & Kozhevnikov, M. (2009). The new object-spatial-verbal cognitive style model: Theory and measurement. Applied Cognitive Psychology, 23(5), 638-663. https://doi.org/10.1002/acp.1473

NIEQ item text: Heavey, C. L., Moynihan, S. A., Brouwers, V. P., Lapping-Carr, L., Krumm, A. E., Kelsey, J. M., Turner, D. K., & Hurlburt, R. T. (2019). Measuring the frequency of inner-experience characteristics by self-report: The Nevada Inner Experience Questionnaire. Frontiers in Psychology, 9, 2615. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2018.02615
usageInfo: VVIQ, OSIVQ, and NIEQ item wording is copyrighted by the original scale authors and is not reproduced here. Item columns below are identified by their official item number/dimension; consult the source publications above for exact wording.

hasPart.name: all_data_surveys
hasPart.description: One row per participant: demographics, questionnaire scores, and raw questionnaire/strategy items.

variableMeasured.name: id
variableMeasured.description: Participant identifier, unique within a version.

variableMeasured.name: version
variableMeasured.description: WM-FTT task version.

levels.v2: Added a parity-error penalty to recall scoring
levels.v3: Added recall-order randomisation; independent front-end infrastructure

variableMeasured.name: language
variableMeasured.description: UI language of the experiment in the browser.

variableMeasured.name: age
variableMeasured.description: Participant age in years, self-reported.

variableMeasured.name: gender
variableMeasured.description: Gender, as freely typed by the participant.
variableMeasured.notes: Free text, not a controlled vocabulary; values include both short codes ("f", "m") and longer self-descriptions in French and English (e.g. "Non-binaire", "female/agender"). Left as-is rather than collapsed into fixed categories, since collapsing would lose information some participants specifically chose to add. No missing values in the current data.

variableMeasured.name: vviq_total_score
variableMeasured.description: Total score on the Vividness of Visual Imagery Questionnaire (VVIQ; Marks, 1973), summed across all 16 items (see vviq_q01- vviq_q16 below). Lower scores indicate weaker/absent visual imagery.
variableMeasured.notes: Missing for 2 participants (of 116).

variableMeasured.name: vviq_group_2
variableMeasured.description: Categorical VVIQ group with 2 levels, based on standard VVIQ cutoff.

variableMeasured.name: vviq_group_4
variableMeasured.description: Categorical VVIQ group with 4 levels, based on standard VVIQ cutoffs.

variableMeasured.name: nieq_mental_imagery
variableMeasured.description: Nevada Inner Experience Questionnaire (NIEQ; Heavey et al., 2019) mental imagery dimension score: mean of the frequency and proportion items for this dimension (see nieq_freq_mental_imagery / nieq_prop_mental_imagery in the nested item columns).
variableMeasured.notes: No missing values.

variableMeasured.name: nieq_inner_voice
variableMeasured.description: NIEQ inner voice/speaking dimension score (mean of frequency and proportion items).
variableMeasured.notes: No missing values.

variableMeasured.name: nieq_emotions
variableMeasured.description: NIEQ feelings/emotions dimension score (mean of frequency and proportion items).
variableMeasured.notes: No missing values.

variableMeasured.name: nieq_sensory_focus
variableMeasured.description: NIEQ sensory awareness dimension score (mean of frequency and proportion items).
variableMeasured.notes: No missing values.

variableMeasured.name: nieq_unsymbolised
variableMeasured.description: NIEQ unsymbolized thinking dimension score (mean of frequency and proportion items).
variableMeasured.notes: No missing values.

variableMeasured.name: object_mean
variableMeasured.description: OSIVQ (Blazhenkova & Kozhevnikov, 2009) object-imagery subscale mean.
variableMeasured.notes: Missing for 2 participants (same 2 as vviq_total_score).

variableMeasured.name: spatial_mean
variableMeasured.description: OSIVQ spatial-imagery subscale mean.
variableMeasured.notes: Missing for 2 participants (same 2 as vviq_total_score).

variableMeasured.name: verbal_mean
variableMeasured.description: OSIVQ verbal cognitive-style subscale mean.
variableMeasured.notes: Missing for 2 participants (same 2 as vviq_total_score).

variableMeasured.name: feedback_total_score_word
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Cumulative word points shown to the participant at the end of the task, summed across trials. Derived from the front end's defective edit distance; see live_diff_word. For analysis use score_word, aggregated as the question requires.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_total_score_angle
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Cumulative orientation points shown at the end of the task. For analysis use score_angle.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_total_score_color
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Cumulative colour points shown at the end of the task. For analysis use score_color.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_total_score
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Combined total points shown to the participant, across all three features and all trials, including the parity penalty in v2 and v3. This is the number participants were told to maximise, so it is meaningful as an account of what they were optimising, but it is not a performance measure.

variableMeasured.name: prognosis
variableMeasured.description: Self-reported aphantasia status/prognosis, where collected.

variableMeasured.name: neuro_trouble
variableMeasured.description: Self-reported neurological condition, freely typed.
variableMeasured.notes: Free text (French), not a controlled vocabulary, e.g. "TDAH", "TSA", "depression suite a un burnout". NA throughout for v3 (not asked in that version's demographics form); collected for v1/v2 only.

variableMeasured.name: treatment
variableMeasured.description: Self-reported relevant treatment.
variableMeasured.notes: NA throughout for v3 (not asked in that version's demographics form); collected for v1/v2 only.

variableMeasured.name: osivq_q01s
variableMeasured.description: OSIVQ item, Spatial scale. Item wording not reproduced; see Blazhenkova & Kozhevnikov (2009).
variableMeasured.notes: 1 = totally disagree; 5 = totally agree. Missing for 2 participants overall. IMPORTANT: reverse-keyed items are stored inconsistently across versions. v1 and v2 store osivq_q02v, osivq_q09v, osivq_q41v and osivq_q42s UNREVERSED; v3 stores them already reversed. The object_mean / spatial_mean / verbal_mean subscale scores are correct in both cases; only these raw item columns differ. Recomputing subscale scores or reliabilities from the items, without reversing them for v1/v2, gives wrong answers: Cronbach's alpha for the verbal subscale comes out at 0.25 instead of 0.84.

hasPart.name: all_data_full
hasPart.description: One row per stimulus: trial structure, targets, responses, timing, and per-trial scores. id, version, language, age, gender, vviq_total_score, vviq_group_2, vviq_group_4, nieq_mental_imagery, nieq_inner_voice, nieq_emotions, nieq_sensory_focus, nieq_unsymbolised, object_mean, spatial_mean, and verbal_mean are the same participant-level columns described in all_data_surveys above, repeated on every stimulus row for this participant. See all_data_surveys for their descriptions, ranges, and missingness.

variableMeasured.name: expe_phase
variableMeasured.description: Task phase this stimulus belongs to.

variableMeasured.name: trial_number
variableMeasured.description: Trial index (1 tutorial + 3 training + 21 test trials per participant).

variableMeasured.name: response_order
variableMeasured.description: Order in which the three response modalities (word/angle/colour) were collected for this trial.
variableMeasured.notes: Fixed at word_angle_color in v1/v2 (always that order); randomised per trial in v3, so all 6 permutations appear.

variableMeasured.name: item_number
variableMeasured.description: Stimulus index within the trial (1-3: word, orientation, colour).

variableMeasured.name: target_word
variableMeasured.description: The to-be-remembered word for this stimulus.

variableMeasured.name: target_angle
variableMeasured.description: The to-be-remembered rectangle orientation, in degrees.

variableMeasured.name: target_color_angle
variableMeasured.description: The to-be-remembered colour, as an angle on the colour wheel used for continuous colour report.

variableMeasured.name: target_color
variableMeasured.description: The to-be-remembered colour, as its nearest named colour.

variableMeasured.name: response_word
variableMeasured.description: Participant's recalled word.

variableMeasured.name: response_angle
variableMeasured.description: Participant's recalled rectangle orientation, in degrees.

variableMeasured.name: response_color_angle
variableMeasured.description: Participant's recalled colour, as an angle on the colour wheel.

variableMeasured.name: response_color
variableMeasured.description: Participant's recalled colour, as its nearest named colour.

variableMeasured.name: score_word
variableMeasured.description: Word recall similarity, 1 = exact match. Edit-distance scoring (Gonthier, 2022): Damerau-Levenshtein distance capped at the target's length, subtracted from it, divided by it. Computed in R from the raw target and response, not from the task's own feedback columns. WARNING: word recall is near ceiling in this task and its split-half reliability is 0.45, below the conventional floor; it does not support individual-differences claims. See the Scoring page of the package documentation.

variableMeasured.name: score_angle
variableMeasured.description: Orientation recall similarity, 1 = exact match. Cosine of the angular error on a 180-degree period, since a rectangle's tilt is symmetric under 180-degree rotation. Split-half reliability 0.82.

variableMeasured.name: score_color
variableMeasured.description: Colour recall similarity, 1 = exact match. Cosine of the angular error on the 360-degree hue wheel. Split-half reliability 0.83.

variableMeasured.name: score_word_z
variableMeasured.description: score_word, z-scored within task version using experimental-block rows only. Retained alongside the raw score: raw for absolute performance, standardised for cross-feature comparison.

variableMeasured.name: score_angle_z
variableMeasured.description: score_angle, z-scored within task version. See score_word_z.

variableMeasured.name: score_color_z
variableMeasured.description: score_color, z-scored within task version. See score_word_z.

variableMeasured.name: responded_word
variableMeasured.description: Whether the participant entered a word at all. IMPORTANT: the task encodes non-response with sentinels rather than missing values, and non-responses are scored 0 in score_word. Analyses of recall accuracy should filter on this flag; analyses that leave it out are combining accuracy with willingness to respond, which are different quantities. See the Scoring page of the package documentation.

variableMeasured.name: responded_angle
variableMeasured.description: Whether the participant moved the orientation widget. NOTE: unlike the other two features this is an inference, not an observation. The widget starts at 90 degrees and returns that value if untouched, so a deliberate 90-degree response is indistinguishable from no response. No block target lies within 20 degrees of 90, so such a response can never be near-correct. See responded_word.

variableMeasured.name: responded_color
variableMeasured.description: Whether the participant moved the colour wheel. Non-response is marked in the raw data by response_color_angle == 999 and response_color '#AAAAAA'. See responded_word.

variableMeasured.name: live_diff_word
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Word recall dissimilarity as computed by the task's front end to drive its feedback screen, 0 = exact match. Note this runs opposite to score_word. WARNING: the front end's edit distance is defective (a loop whose condition is an assignment leaves the distance matrix half-initialised), so this is not a valid edit distance. Retained for provenance only. See the Scoring page.

variableMeasured.name: live_diff_angle
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Absolute orientation error divided by 180, as computed by the front end, 0 = exact match. Linear rather than cosine, and with no handling of the rectangle's 180-degree symmetry. Use score_angle instead.

variableMeasured.name: live_diff_color
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Circular colour error divided by 180, as computed by the front end, 0 = exact match. Non-responses are mapped to 1 by an explicit guard. Use score_color instead.

variableMeasured.name: rt_word
variableMeasured.description: Response time for the word recall response.

variableMeasured.name: rt_angle
variableMeasured.description: Response time for the orientation recall response.

variableMeasured.name: rt_color
variableMeasured.description: Response time for the colour recall response.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_score_word
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Points shown on the feedback screen for the word response (0, 0.5 or 1), thresholded from live_diff_word and therefore inheriting its defective edit distance. Use score_word.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_score_angle
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Points shown for the orientation response (0, 0.5 or 1). Use score_angle.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_score_color
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Points shown for the colour response (0, 0.5 or 1). Use score_color.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_trial_score
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Points shown for the whole trial: the sum of the three per-feature feedback scores, minus 0.5 per incorrect parity judgement, floored at 0. Trial-level, so constant across the three stimulus rows of a trial. The parity penalty applies in v2 and v3 only.

variableMeasured.name: parity_1_stim
variableMeasured.description: First of the two parity-judgement distractor digits embedded in this trial.

variableMeasured.name: parity_1_resp
variableMeasured.description: Participant's parity judgement (odd/even) for parity_1_stim.

variableMeasured.name: parity_1_acc
variableMeasured.description: Accuracy of the first parity judgement (1 = correct, 0 = incorrect).

variableMeasured.name: parity_1_rt
variableMeasured.description: Response time for the first parity judgement.

variableMeasured.name: parity_2_stim
variableMeasured.description: Second of the two parity-judgement distractor digits embedded in this trial.

variableMeasured.name: parity_2_resp
variableMeasured.description: Participant's parity judgement (odd/even) for parity_2_stim.

variableMeasured.name: parity_2_acc
variableMeasured.description: Accuracy of the second parity judgement (1 = correct, 0 = incorrect).

variableMeasured.name: parity_2_rt
variableMeasured.description: Response time for the second parity judgement.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_total_score_word
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Cumulative word points shown to the participant at the end of the task. Derived from the front end's defective edit distance; see live_diff_word. Use score_word.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_total_score_angle
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Cumulative orientation points shown at the end of the task. Use score_angle.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_total_score_color
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Cumulative colour points shown at the end of the task. Use score_color.

variableMeasured.name: feedback_total_score
variableMeasured.description: DISPLAY ONLY, NOT FOR ANALYSIS. Combined total points shown to the participant, including the parity penalty in v2 and v3. This is the number participants were told to maximise, so it is meaningful as an account of what they were optimising, but it is not a performance measure.

variableMeasured.name: prognosis
variableMeasured.description: Self-reported aphantasia status/prognosis, where collected.

variableMeasured.name: neuro_trouble
variableMeasured.description: Self-reported neurological condition, freely typed.
variableMeasured.notes: Free text (French), not a controlled vocabulary. NA throughout for v3.

variableMeasured.name: treatment
variableMeasured.description: Self-reported relevant treatment.
variableMeasured.notes: NA throughout for v3.
